one_liner: Yandex's eBPF continuous CPU profiler that unwinds frame-pointer-less native stacks in-kernel; a perf record alternative, no measured win.
what_it_does: A fleet-wide continuous profiling system: a per-node agent samples kernel and userspace stacks with eBPF on perf_events (by default one atomic pprof profile per pod per minute) and ships them over gRPC to stateless storage and symbolizer services backed by ClickHouse, PostgreSQL and S3, with a web UI, query language and AutoFDO/sPGO profile export. It also ships a standalone `perforator record` CLI that profiles a command, a PID or the whole host and writes pprof or a flamegraph HTML, which is the part that competes with `perf record`. It is not a library and not a drop-in for perf's CLI or data format.
how_it_is_fast: The agent precompiles each binary's .eh_frame into unwind rules stored in BPF maps as a 3-level page table (4136-byte pages, 256 rules per leaf), so the eBPF program can unwind code built without frame pointers inside the kernel instead of copying raw stack to userspace as `perf --call-graph dwarf` does. Symbolization is moved off the hosts: binaries are uploaded once per build-id and symbolized centrally (GSYM), so each node does not repeat the expensive DWARF work. No measurement of the resulting overhead against perf is published.
when_to_use: Always-on CPU profiling across a Kubernetes fleet of C++, C, Go or Rust services where binaries are built without -fno-omit-frame-pointer.
You need central storage and query over months of profiles, merged across many pods, with diffing in a UI.
Feeding sPGO/AutoFDO (and LBR-based) profiles from production back into PGO builds.
Ad-hoc local profiling of a command or PID on x86-64 Linux 5.4+ via `perforator record` when perf's DWARF mode produces too much data.
when_not_to_use: aarch64 or non-Linux hosts: the docs say x86-64 is the only supported architecture.
You need hardware counter breakdowns, tracepoints, perf script/annotate workflows or anything beyond CPU stack sampling; perf does far more event types (kprobe support is an open issue).
Environments that cannot grant CAP_SYS_ADMIN (CAP_BPF-only operation is an open request) or kernels without BTF.
You want evidence of lower overhead than perf: the only figures are system requirements (512Mb RAM, <1% of host CPUs), not a measured comparison.
Small teams that do not want to run ClickHouse, PostgreSQL and S3 just for profiling; use the CLI or perf instead.

integration.form: Go/C binaries (agent, CLI, microservices) plus Helm chart; not a library
integration.dependencies: eBPF-capable kernel with BTF; full deployment needs ClickHouse, PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage; build uses yatool (Python 3.12+) and compiles LLVM internals (~10 GiB disk)
integration.min_toolchain: Linux 5.4+ (5.7+ and Intel CPU for LBR profiles); build via ./ya make or Docker
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — `perforator record` covers perf record's CPU flamegraph use case with different flags and pprof/HTML output, not perf.data

gotchas: Needs debug symbols (in the binary or via debuginfod) and an .eh_frame section; builds with -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables cannot be unwound, and .debug_frame support is an open issue.
Newest non-LTS kernels may break the eBPF program because it reads evolving kernel structures; the docs say they test LTS kernels after 5.4. An open issue reports a kernel panic.
The DWARF unwinder stops at 128 frames, and an open issue reports detached frames for a C++ ECS dispatch despite complete .eh_frame and frame pointers.
The agent uploads every executable it finds on profiled nodes to central storage; the eBPF unwinder and JVM code are GPL-2.0 while the rest is Apache-2.0.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over magic-trace when you want low-rate sampling of a whole fleet with central storage rather than a few-millisecond Intel PT trace of one process; pick bpftime or funtrace only for instrumentation, which Perforator does not do.
verified_claims_summary: There is no benchmark: the README states the agent uses 512Mb of RAM (more on large hosts) and under 1% of host CPUs and profiles 'without affecting' performance, and a maintainer discussion argues lower overhead than on-agent symbolizers without numbers, so no ratio against perf exists.
status_note: Actively maintained by Yandex (recent commits are automated syncs, 34 open issues) and deployed on tens of thousands of servers, but it is a multi-service system to operate, not code to copy.
